protocol.question: Do frozen latent-dynamical co-participation edges improve a normalized physical-node GNN on noisy LJ trajectories?
protocol.base_graph: the frozen AE noisy-LJ graph, including mandatory graph-distance-two/three augmentation
protocol.influence_definition: For each initial global-latent basis direction, estimate the centered perturbation response [decode(F^k(z+epsilon))-decode(F^k(z-epsilon))]/(2 epsilon), with epsilon=0.001 in normalized latent units. Concatenate absolute node response vectors over k=5,10,20 and score node pairs by their Gram product. Select the symmetric union of each node's top-four nonphysical partners.
protocol.limitation: The accepted simulator has one global 2D latent, not per-node latent variables. These are shared learned-mode participation edges, not a literal per-node latent Jacobian.
protocol.random_control: For every network, sample exactly as many nonphysical edges as its latent arm, using a deterministic graph-specific seed.

downstream_model.node_inputs: current displacement plus three velocity histories
downstream_model.edge_inputs: reference/current relative vectors and lengths, stretch, stiffness, physical-edge indicator, added-edge indicator
downstream_model.normalization: training-only feature/target standardization plus LayerNorm in encoders and every residual message block
